::: {.callout-note title="Work in progress"}
This optional track adds engineering mathematics and modelling to regular Computer Engineering Technology work. It is locally developed, is not endorsed by a college or university, and does not guarantee admission or postsecondary credit. New assignments and the thermal-process project still require development and classroom testing.
:::

## The pathway

Work through the chapters in order. Each chapter connects mathematics to circuits, computers, programming, measurement, energy, or control. Existing lessons and activities are linked where they are ready.

### Chapter 0: Engineering baseline and notebook

**Learning goal:** Assess current algebra, units, graphing, estimation, calculator, and technical-writing skills, then establish a consistent engineering notebook format.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Engineering solutions must show the model, assumptions, equations, units, checks, and revisions—not only a final number. The diagnostic identifies skills to review before the analytical work begins.
:::

**Deliverable:** Unmarked diagnostic, correction record, learning targets, and notebook setup.

### Chapter 1: Quantities, units, and scale

**Learning goal:** Use dimensional analysis, engineering notation, significant figures, ratios, rates, estimates, and compound units.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Units and estimates expose impossible calculator results. These habits transfer directly to every engineering discipline.
:::

**Start with:** [Number Systems, Measurement, Units, and Calculator Skills](../01-number-systems/index.qmd)
**Deliverable:** Assignment 1—quantity and unit audit.
**References:** [[1, Ch. 0]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[27, Ch. 1]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) [[28, Chs. 1, 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 2: Algebraic electrical models

**Learning goal:** Rearrange electrical equations, identify proportional and inverse relationships, and apply physical limits to a design.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Engineers must build and manipulate models rather than only substitute numbers into formulas. Physical limits separate a mathematical answer from a workable design.
:::

**Start with:** [Charge, Voltage, and Current](../02-basic-electronics/01-charge-voltage-current.qmd), [Closed, Open, and Short Circuits](../02-basic-electronics/02-circuits-opens-shorts.qmd), and [Ohm's Law](../02-basic-electronics/03-ohms-law.qmd).
**Deliverable:** Assignment 2—resistive design brief, after the [Basic Circuit Calculations worksheet](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/TEJ_Basic_Circuit_Calculations_Student_Worksheet.pdf).
**Reference:** [[1, Chs. 1, 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

### Chapter 3: Series and parallel networks

**Learning goal:** Derive and apply the current, voltage, resistance, and power rules for series, parallel, and mixed circuits.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Circuit rules are examples of conservation and equivalent modelling. Independent checks make a solution defensible.
:::

**Deliverable:** Assignment 3—series-parallel design proof.
**Reference:** [[1, Chs. 4–6]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

### Chapter 4: Coupled equations and Kirchhoff's laws

**Learning goal:** Form and solve two- and three-variable linear systems from branch, node, and loop equations, then verify the result.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Coupled equations appear in circuits, structures, processes, controls, and data models. Residual and power checks show whether the complete model is consistent.
:::

**Deliverable:** Assignment 4—branch-current system solved by hand and checked with software.
**References:** [[1, Chs. 7, 9]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 9, 12]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 5: Equivalent models and optimization

**Learning goal:** Replace a network with a useful terminal model and compare designs using constraints, sensitivity, efficiency, safety, and cost.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Engineering decisions rarely have one perfect answer. Maximum power, maximum efficiency, minimum cost, and lowest temperature may require different designs.
:::

**Deliverable:** Assignment 5—source and load optimization memo.
**References:** [[1, Ch. 10]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 13–16]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 6: Power and energy balances

**Learning goal:** Define a system boundary and use input, output, accumulation, loss, and efficiency to model electrical and thermal energy.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Energy balances connect electronics to computer, mechanical, chemical, and environmental systems. Comparing input with stored energy also introduces loss and model calibration.
:::

**Start with:** [Power and Energy](../02-basic-electronics/04-power-energy.qmd) and the [Computer Power and Parts mission](../computer-systems/computer-power-parts.qmd).
**Deliverables:** Assignment 6—energy audit; Lab 1—supervised low-voltage thermal balance.
**References:** [[1, Chs. 1, 12]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[27, Chs. 3, 5–6]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008)

::: {.callout-important title="Safety boundary"}
Use only teacher-approved protected low-voltage equipment. Students do not construct or probe mains circuits. Isolate liquids from exposed electronics and define temperature, current, containment, and shutdown limits before testing.
:::

### Chapter 7: Measurement, calibration, and uncertainty

**Learning goal:** Collect repeatable data, fit a suitable model, inspect residuals, and state its valid range and uncertainty.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Measurements become useful evidence only when their limits are understood. Calibration and uncertainty affect every engineering discipline.
:::

**Deliverable:** Lab 2—sensor calibration and model check.
**References:** [[1, Ch. 8]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 3, 4, 17, 20]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 8: Transient and step-by-step systems

**Learning goal:** Model an electrical or thermal system that changes with time using a time constant or a step-by-step spreadsheet or program.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Real systems take time to charge, heat, cool, accelerate, and settle. Numerical stepping builds intuition for later differential-equation models.
:::

**Deliverable:** Assignment 7—resistor-capacitor or thermal transient model.
**References:** [[1, Chs. 16, 18–22]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Ch. 25]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 9: Logic, algorithms, and state

**Learning goal:** Translate logic, equations, and state behaviour into truth tables, algorithms, tested programs, and state-transition diagrams.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Programming makes a model repeatable and testable. Truth tables and state machines bridge mathematical conditions and safe embedded-system behaviour.
:::

**Start with:** [Digital Logic and Stable Inputs](../03-digital-logic-inputs/index.qmd) and the [Digital Inputs worksheet](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/D01_Digital_Inputs_Student_Worksheet.pdf).
**Deliverables:** Assignment 8—engineering calculation program; Assignment 9—safety state machine.
**Reference:** [[28, Ch. 2]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 10: Electromechanical systems

**Learning goal:** Relate electrical input to torque, speed, motion or flow, mechanical power, efficiency, and safe operating limits.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Motors, pumps, fans, and actuators join electrical and mechanical systems. Current, temperature, speed, load, and efficiency cannot all be optimized independently.
:::

**Deliverable:** Lab 3—actuator characterization.
**Reference:** [[1, Chs. 13–14]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

### Chapter 11: Feedback, models, and design decisions

**Learning goal:** Compare open-loop, on-off, hysteresis, proportional, proportional-integral, and proportional-integral-derivative control using common response evidence.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
Feedback responds to disturbances but introduces trade-offs involving speed, overshoot, error, saturation, stability, and safety.
:::

**Start with:** [Control Systems and Computer Numerical Control](../05-control-systems/index.qmd).
**Deliverable:** Assignment 10—control-method comparison, using the [Control Methods Comparison handout](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/C06_Control_Methods_Comparison_Student.pdf).
**References:** [[27, Ch. 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) [[28, Chs. 16, 20]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

### Chapter 12: Integrated engineering project

**Learning goal:** Design, model, build or simulate, program, measure, validate, revise, and explain an instrumented system.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why it matters"}
The project brings mathematical reasoning, construction, safety, data, programming, and communication into one engineering workflow. Strong work includes evidence of revision, not just a working prototype.
:::

**Recommended project:** Instrumented low-voltage thermal process controller. Alternatives may include a motor or pump test stand, battery and thermal monitor, controlled fan system, tank-level simulator, or renewable-energy demonstrator.
**Deliverable:** Project 1—requirements, model, schematic, build or approved simulation, code, validation, revision, and concise technical report.

## Core references

The textbooks are teacher references. Public activities use original explanations, diagrams, values, and questions.

[[1]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) **Grob's Basic Electronics, 12th edition** supports electronics, measurement, circuit analysis, energy, electromagnetism, and transient circuits.

[[27]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) **Çengel, Introduction to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, 2nd edition** supports units, energy balances, closed systems, control volumes, heat transfer, and transient thermal behaviour.

[[28]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) **Chapra and Canale, Numerical Methods for Engineers, 6th edition** supports modelling, error, linear systems, optimization, curve fitting, programming, and numerical time-step models.
